increment_paragraph: **CELL-PROTOCOL-CLOSE-ACTUAL** (gateway rule 38d, registered by MK-EVENT-CELL-CROSS-FUNCTION; USER DECISION 2026-11-02, verbatim: "B as recommended", Q3: a close of a declared cell member is that cell's `#stale`): the access gate (W44-INDIRECT-CALL-ARGUMENT-ACCESS premise 1) refused the integer member actual of `close(r->CELL)` at close's custody position, so rule 38c's close was never the statement's custody effect. Rule 38d admits exactly that actual: rule 38 in force; a statement whose lowering is exactly the gate's refusal and that is rule 38c's close of a declared record's one-segment cell; a function-map callee releasing its one actual with kind `descriptor`; the actual exactly the integer member read `r->F` or a constant in-bounds element `r->F[K]` of that cell. It lowers to the actual's typed read and second obligation, the call with its released position read as `Borrowed`, and rule 38c's close marked admitted, which is the statement's whole custody effect: a live single identity is staled once, a stale, maybe, joined or unrecorded cell refuses (`descriptor-cell-double-release`, `descriptor-cell-undecided`), and where the path holds no fact of a caller's record the gate's refusal stands. An undeclared record, a non-cell member, a multi-segment cell, a copied number (Q4), a used result, a non-release position, a heap kind, an uncontracted callee (Windows `closesocket` has none) and rule 38 off keep the gate's refusal byte for byte. Package `rule-38-descriptor-cells::close_actual` (`admits`, `reading`, shared vectors; registry arm `descriptor-cell-close-actual`); Lean `QCore.CellProtocolCloseActual` (14 theorems: the admission set is exactly the stated one, an admitted close is the cell's `#stale` and never a silent release, two admitted closes and the sentinel's dead store restore the protocol); 27 fixtures (`tests/cell_protocol_close_actual.rs`), and `descriptor_cell_protocols.rs`'s close test now expects `Safe`. No production declaration carries a `quant cell` protocol at this card's tip, so the prediction is `none` on every route; with CELL-PROTOCOL-FB-DECLARATIONS the admitted closes are read at the declared ends but refuse there (each end tested by its own `> 0`, no sentinel store), so no status move is expected (follow-up CELL-PROTOCOL-PER-END-GUARDS). Report: docs/reports/cell-protocol-close-actual/README.md.

ledger.why: DISCHARGED by CELL-PROTOCOL-CLOSE-ACTUAL (gateway rule 38d, docs/reports/cell-protocol-close-actual/README.md): the access gate admits exactly an integer member read (or constant in-bounds element) of a declared protocol record's one-segment cell at the descriptor-kind release position of a function-map callee, in a statement that is exactly rule 38c's close, with that close marked admitted as the statement's whole custody effect (a live single identity staled once; otherwise rule 38c's refusal, or the gate's where rule 38c reads nothing; never a silent release). Fixtures for every admitted and refused shape (`close` and `mk_event_closesocket`; Windows `closesocket` has no contract and keeps the refusal) in crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/cell_protocol_close_actual.rs, `a_close_of_a_protocol_cell_leaves_the_access_gate` in descriptor_cell_protocols.rs, Lean QCore.CellProtocolCloseActual, and a declared measurement (`none` on corpus, system and slice: no production protocol at the tip).

ledger.text: AMENDED (CELL-PROTOCOL-CLOSE-ACTUAL, 2026-11-02, docs/reports/cell-protocol-close-actual/README.md): the access gate's refusal at a declared cell's `close(r->CELL)` is discharged (rule 38d: the actual is admitted for rule 38c's close). What stays for descriptor cells' ends: Fluent Bit's destroyers test each channel end with its own `> 0` and store no sentinel after closing (flb_output_instance_destroy, flb_input_instance_destroy, input_thread_instance_destroy), and a G05i protocol has one guard per record, so the second end's close stays `descriptor-cell-undecided` and the record `descriptor-cell-protocol-broken` at the exit, and a record holding two channel pairs (ch_events beside ingress_queue_channels, ch_parent_events beside ch_thread_events) declares only one (CELL-PROTOCOL-PER-END-GUARDS); flb_engine_failed's `[1] != [0]` guard is no protocol test, so its close keeps the gate's refusal.

ledger.title: A channel end tested by its own sentinel is not read under a G05i protocol
ledger.text: Registered by CELL-PROTOCOL-CLOSE-ACTUAL. Rule 38d admits `close(r->CELL)` of a declared cell for rule 38c's close, but Fluent Bit's destroyers close each end under its own test (`if (ins->ch_events[1] > 0) mk_event_closesocket(ins->ch_events[1]);`, flb_output.c:619-621, flb_input.c:1315-1317, flb_input_thread.c:212-222 at 046accf6/34155955) and store no sentinel after the closes. A G05i protocol has one guard per record and says nothing of a non-guard cell's value where the guard is dead, so on the guard's dead edge the second end's close names no live descriptor (`descriptor-cell-undecided`) and the record is `descriptor-cell-protocol-broken` at the exit (tests/cell_protocol_close_actual.rs `fluent_bits_output_instance_ends_refuse_after_admission`); and a record with two channel pairs (flb_input_instance: ch_events, ingress_queue_channels; flb_input_thread_instance: ch_parent_events, ch_thread_events, notification_channels) can declare only one protocol. DISCHARGE: a user decision on per-end sentinels (each cell its own guard) or several protocols per record, its grammar and rule 38c reading with Lean parity, fixtures for each Fluent Bit end, and a declared measurement.
